title: Matching thread to canvas count
subtitle: How to pick the right wool or cotton for any canvas count
excerpt: The thread must fill the canvas holes without forcing. Too thin and the canvas shows; too thick and the thread bunches and pulls. Three thread families cover all standard canvas counts: Persian wool, tapestry wool, and stranded cotton.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), thread selection chapter. Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), thread and canvas sections.

glossaryTerms.definition: A three-strand wool thread. The strands can be separated so you use one, two, or three strands to match different canvas counts.
A single-strand heavier wool thread. Used at full weight on 10 to 13-count canvas. Not designed to be separated.
A twisted, tightly spun cotton thread with a slight sheen. Comes in numbered sizes; size 5 is medium weight, size 8 is finer.

heroPrompt: Three skeins of needlepoint thread side by side: Persian wool, tapestry wool, and perle cotton in coordinating tones, with swatches of 10-count and 13-count canvas behind, natural light.

content.text: The correct thread for a canvas count fills each hole fully without forcing through. If you can see canvas threads between your stitches when the work lies flat, add a strand. If the thread is hard to draw through the hole or puckers the canvas, reduce a strand.

comes in three separable strands. On 13-count canvas, use one strand. On 10-count canvas, use two strands. On 18-count canvas, use half a strand: technically one strand from a thinner-weight Persian, or substitute a fine wool or cotton.
is a single-strand heavier wool. One strand suits 13-count canvas well. Two strands suit 10-count. Tapestry wool is not intended to be separated, so it works on fewer counts than Persian wool.
and stranded cotton suit 18-count and finer. Size 5 perle on 13-count canvas. Stranded cotton, two to three strands, on 18-count.
10-count canvas: two strands Persian wool, or one strand tapestry wool. Tapestry needle size 18.
13-count canvas: one strand Persian wool, or two strands tapestry wool. Tapestry needle size 20.
18-count canvas: one strand fine wool, or two to three strands of stranded cotton. Tapestry needle size 22.

Work a small test swatch of five to ten stitches in the corner of the canvas. Hold the swatch up to a lamp. If any canvas threads show between the stitches, add a strand. If the needle pulls hard through the holes, remove a strand. The test swatch takes two minutes and saves an hour of re-working.

Cut thread no longer than 45 cm for wool. Longer lengths develop a hairy, worn look from the friction of passing repeatedly through the canvas. Bargello stitches, which are long and upright, can take 60 cm because each stitch uses more thread per pass.
